Functional demographic model of Hyndman and Ullah (demography)

Source: R/model-wrappers.R
hyndman_ullah.Rd

Wrapper around demography::fdm() (Hyndman and Ullah 2007): the rates of each year are smoothed over age with demography::smooth.demogdata() (smooth = TRUE, by default monotonic regression splines above age 65, weighted by the exposures), the log rates are decomposed into a mean function and principal components, and the scores are forecast with ARIMA or ETS models. Draws are simulated with demography's simulate() method for functional forecasts (uncertainty of the coefficients and resampled model errors). Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add Poisson variation of the deaths given the rates and the exposures, as for other models of expected rates, and no other observation noise. If intervals are too narrow on real data, that is a property of the model (see recalibrated(), ensemble(), or overdispersed models such as stanmomo(family = "nb")).

Usage

hyndman_ullah(
  order = 6,
  method = "arima",
  smooth = TRUE,
  smooth_args = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

order

Number of principal components.

method

Forecast method for the coefficients ("arima", "ets", "rwdrift", ...), passed to forecast().

smooth

Smooth the rates of each year over age before the decomposition.

smooth_args

List of arguments of demography::smooth.demogdata() (for example list(k = 20) or list(method = "spline")).

...

Further arguments of demography::fdm().

Value

A model specification.

Details

Without smoothing, the model errors that simulate() resamples contain the observation noise, which predictive draws then add a second time (as Poisson variation): keep smooth = TRUE unless the rates were smoothed in a preprocessing step. smooth.demogdata() works on single years of age; for age groups the smoothed values at the observed ages are used (a weaker smoothing). The smoothing settings (smooth_args, such as k, the number of knots) and the number of components can be chosen by forecast accuracy with tuned(). When the default monotonic spline cannot be fitted (for example for age ranges that start in middle age), the rates are smoothed without the monotonicity constraint and the fit diagnostics say so.

References

Hyndman RJ, Ullah MS (2007). Robust forecasting of mortality and fertility rates: a functional data approach. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis 51(10): 4942-4956.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("demography", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1995:2019)
  fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(hyndman_ullah(order = 2), x), h = 5, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
}
